raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Fixes #61383: when the residual `max(p - q, 0)` is tiny, MRV2 rejection sampling now resamples a token from the target's support instead of token 0.

When the draft puts almost all of its mass on the only token the target allows, fp32 rounds the residual to zero, and the resample emits token 0. This PR keeps the residual nonzero in fp32. It complements #64242 / #65103, which fix only the global log-sum-exp layer (see Details).

## Claims

- The rejected position samples from the target's support for draft gaps up to ~87. Before, it emitted token 0 (`!`) from gap ≈ 14 on, matching the issue's `grammar rejected tokens [756, 414, 0]`.
- All math stays in fp32. There is no fp64 math and no fallback path.
- Standard and block verification are both fixed.

## Validation

Regression test `test_resample_stays_in_target_support` (draft gap ∈ {10, 14, 25} × block verification on/off). At the rejected position, the target allows a single token; the draft puts all but `exp(-gap)` of its mass on that token, and the rejected draft token lies outside the target's support.

On base `f9db1756e9`, RTX 2050:

```text
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py -k resample_stays   # kernel unmodified
E       assert [1, 2, 0] == [1, 2, 3]
FAILED ...::test_resample_stays_in_target_support[14.0-False]
FAILED ...::test_resample_stays_in_target_support[14.0-True]
FAILED ...::test_resample_stays_in_target_support[25.0-False]
FAILED ...::test_resample_stays_in_target_support[25.0-True]
4 failed, 2 passed

$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_rejection_sampler_utils.py   # this PR
101 passed
```

The issue's own setup does not reproduce reliably at the server level; see the issue thread. To check the actual failing state end to end, a standalone reproducer rebuilds it with:

- real XGrammar with the Qwen3-4B tokenizer;
- the production grammar-mask path;
- top-k=50 and top-p=0.9;
- draft logits that are not grammar-masked, with a background of -20.

It then runs the actual Triton kernels (base `a1cfd2c1b5`). Block and token verification always give the same result:

| Draft gap | main | #64242 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | OK | OK | OK |
| 14 | emits `!` | OK | OK |
| 18 / 20 / 30 / 80 | emits `!` | emits `!` | OK |

The reproducer was run on an earlier base (`a1cfd2c1b5`); I can share it on request.

With the draft background at `-inf`, so that the residual is exactly `exp(-gap)`, this PR is exact up to gap 87. Below that point `exp(-gap)` falls under fp32's smallest normal number and is flushed to zero on GPU.

**Performance.** End-to-end `rejection_sample` with:

- V = 151,936 and fp32 logits, temperature 1;
- a draft equal to the target plus N(0, 1) noise;
- timing by FlashInfer CUPTI with CUDA graphs: the median of each run, averaged over A/B/A/B runs.

Measured on an RTX 2050 (laptop GPU) on base f9db1756e9. I'll follow up with numbers from a datacenter GPU. In every case below, the accepted lengths and sampled tokens are identical to main.

| verification | requests | K | main µs | this PR µs | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| token | 1 | 3 | 75.3 | 79.2 | +5.2% |
| token | 16 | 3 | 846.8 | 865.0 | +2.1% |
| token | 64 | 7 | 6,721.5 | 6,804.3 | +1.2% |
| block | 1 | 3 | 92.4 | 105.2 | +13.8% |
| block | 16 | 3 | 1,224.0 | 1,240.3 | +1.3% |
| block | 64 | 7 | 11,693.9 | 11,762.3 | +0.6% |

<details><summary>Full matrix and per-kernel breakdown</summary>

End-to-end, all cases:

| block | reqs | K | main µs | this PR µs | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| False | 1 | 3 | 75.3 | 79.2 | +5.2% |
| False | 16 | 3 | 846.8 | 865.0 | +2.1% |
| False | 64 | 3 | 3,262.4 | 3,306.2 | +1.3% |
| False | 1 | 7 | 124.2 | 129.1 | +4.0% |
| False | 16 | 7 | 1,696.4 | 1,725.6 | +1.7% |
| False | 64 | 7 | 6,721.5 | 6,804.3 | +1.2% |
| True | 1 | 3 | 92.4 | 105.2 | +13.8% |
| True | 16 | 3 | 1,224.0 | 1,240.3 | +1.3% |
| True | 64 | 3 | 4,912.0 | 4,951.6 | +0.8% |
| True | 1 | 7 | 217.6 | 225.3 | +3.6% |
| True | 16 | 7 | 2,950.7 | 2,983.2 | +1.1% |
| True | 64 | 7 | 11,693.9 | 11,762.3 | +0.6% |

Per kernel, 64 requests, K = 7 (torch profiler, µs per call):

| kernel | token: main | token: PR | block: main | block: PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel` | 6,014.9 | 6,151.3 (+2.3%) | 6,045.3 | 6,106.3 (+1.0%) |
| `_compute_local_residual_mass_kernel` | – | – | 5,158.9 | 5,162.7 (+0.1%) |
| `_compute_cumulative_log_p_kernel` | – | – | 9.8 | 12.3 (+25%) |
| `_rejection_kernel` | 12.9 | 14.1 | 10.1 | 10.3 |
| `_resample_kernel` | 851.6 | 856.5 (+0.6%) | 808.1 | 811.3 (+0.4%) |

</details>

The cost comes from the per-block max index and the merge's extra `log1p` and `where`. It is under 2.5% wherever the stats pass dominates. The largest relative cost is +12.8 µs at a single request with K = 3 under block verification, where the per-position merges in `_compute_cumulative_log_p_kernel` run serially. Everything stays fp32, so there is no fp64 cost on GPUs with low fp64 throughput.

**Model eval:** to follow in this draft (spec-decode acceptance length and structured-output validity, main vs this PR).

CI: the `V1 Spec Decode` step runs `tests/v1/spec_decode` on NVIDIA and AMD.

## Details

**Root cause.** At the rejected position the target is one-hot on `"`, and `q(") = 1 - exp(-gap)`. Three fp32 steps each round the residual to zero:

| Step | main | Rounds from |
|---|---|---|
| Per-block sumexp | `sum(exp(x - max))`, including the max's own `1` | `1 + exp(-18)` → `1` |
| Global log-sum-exp | `max + log(sumexp)` | `25 + 8.3e-7` → `25` (gap ≈ 14) |
| Residual | `log_p + log1p(-exp(log_q - log_p))` | `exp(-1.5e-8)` → `1` |

With all three rounded away, the residual is `-inf` everywhere, and Gumbel argmax then returns index 0.

**Fix.**

- **The log-sum-exp is carried as `(max, correction)`.** `_compute_global_logsumexp` returns the pair, and `_log_softmax` computes `(x - max) - correction`. The two per-request `*_rejected_logsumexp` buffers passed to `_resample_kernel` become `[num_reqs, 2]`.
- **The stats kernel's per-block sumexp leaves out one max element** (`_compute_max_and_sumexp_excluding_max`; Barron, ["A Fix for Softmax"](https://jonbarron.info/softmaxfix/)). The merge takes `log1p` of the remainder. `_compute_max_and_sumexp` is unchanged because `acceptance_estimator.py` needs the standard sumexp.
- **The residual is `log_p + log(-expm1(log_q - log_p))` when `log_q < log_p`, and `-inf` otherwise.** The `delta < 0` test also covers the `-inf` and NaN cases. The kernel already used libdevice `log1p` here; `expm1` comes from the same library.

All three are needed:

- With the first two, the correction is exact, but gap ≥ 18 still fails at `exp(delta)`.
- `expm1` alone changes nothing, because `log_q` has already rounded to `0`.

**Relation to #64242 / #65103.**

- #64242 promotes the global log-sum-exp to fp64.
- #65103 replaces that with an fp32 `(hi, lo)` pair, which is equivalent to the first bullet above. It also fixes the one-hot residual mass and takes the target log-sum-exp from an fp64 op on the top-p on-load path.

Neither changes the per-block sumexp, which matters here on the draft side, nor the exp(delta) residual. Both still resample token 0 at large gaps:

#64242: the reproducer above emits ! at gap ≥ 18.
#65103 (ae6817425a): test_resample_stays_in_target_support, added unchanged to its test file, passes at gaps 10 and 14 but fails at gap 25 under both standard and block verification, with assert [1, 2, 0] == [1, 2, 3]. The other 134 tests in that file pass on the same setup.

If #65103 lands first, this PR reduces to a small follow-up on it: the stable per-block sumexp, the `expm1` residual and the test. I'm happy to rebase it that way.

**Not changed.**

- `_compute_local_residual_mass_kernel` and the one-hot `_compute_global_residual_mass` still use `exp` followed by a subtraction. They affect the precision of block verification's acceptance threshold, not which tokens can be emitted. #65103 fixes the one-hot case.
- If `p == q` exactly in fp32, the residual is mathematically empty and would need a fallback to sampling from the target. That is out of scope.
- MRV1's `vllm/v1/sample/rejection_sampler.py` was not examined.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate, implement and test this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and the reproducer above myself.

@@ -1290,6 +1290,54 @@ def test_block_verification_accepts_at_least_as_many(num_speculative_steps: int)
     )
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_block_verification", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("draft_gap", [10.0, 14.0, 25.0])
+def test_resample_stays_in_target_support(
+    draft_gap: float, use_block_verification: bool
+):
+    """A resample must come from the target's support.
+
+    Rows 0-1 accept with p_2 == 1. Row 2's target allows only token 3 (grammar
+    plus top-p), and the draft puts all but ~exp(-draft_gap) of its mass there.
+    Draft 2 is token 5: grammar-valid, but outside the target's support, so it
+    is rejected and the residual max(p(x) - q(x), 0) is ~exp(-draft_gap) on
+    token 3 only. fp32 must not round that residual to zero everywhere.
+    """
+    device = "cuda"
+    K = 3
+    num_rows = K + 1
+    vocab_size = 64
+    allowed_token, rejected_draft = 3, 5
+
+    target_logits = torch.full((num_rows, vocab_size), float("-inf"), device=device)
+    target_logits[0, 1] = 0.0
+    target_logits[1, 2] = 0.0
+    target_logits[2, allowed_token] = 0.0
+    target_logits[3, 7] = 0.0
+    draft_logits = torch.full((1, K, vocab_size), -20.0, device=device)
+    draft_logits[0, 0, 1] = 25.0
+    draft_logits[0, 1, 2] = 25.0
+    draft_logits[0, 2, allowed_token] = 25.0
+    draft_logits[0, 2, rejected_draft] = 25.0 - draft_gap
+
+    sampled, num_sampled = _rejection_sample(
+        target_logits=target_logits,
+        draft_logits=draft_logits,
+        draft_sampled=torch.tensor([9, 1, 2, rejected_draft], device=device),
+        cu_num_logits=torch.tensor([0, num_rows], dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        pos=torch.arange(num_rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        idx_mapping=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        expanded_idx_mapping=torch.zeros(num_rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        expanded_local_pos=torch.arange(num_rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        temperature=torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.float32, device=device),
+        seed=torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device=device),
+        num_speculative_steps=K,
+        use_block_verification=use_block_verification,
+    )
+
+    assert sampled[0, : int(num_sampled[0])].tolist() == [1, 2, allowed_token]
+
+
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("has_draft_logits", [True, False])
 @pytest.mark.parametrize("fly_window_size", [0, 2])
 def test_chunked_requests_match_full_batch(

@@ -27,6 +27,16 @@ def _compute_max_and_sumexp(logits):
     return max, sumexp
 
 
+@triton.jit
+def _compute_max_and_sumexp_excluding_max(logits, BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr):
+    # The sum excludes one max element, i.e. its exp(0) = 1, so that the small
+    # remainder is not rounded away by 1 + eps (Barron, "A Fix for Softmax").

👋 Hi! Thank you for contributing to the vLLM project.

💬 Join our developer Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai to discuss your PR in `#pr-reviews`, coordinate on features in `#feat-` channels, or join special interest groups in `#sig-` channels.

PRs do not trigger a full CI run by default. Reviewers with write access and configured trusted contributors can comment `/ci run` for upstream CI or `/amd-ci run` for AMD CI only whenever CI signals are needed.

Once the PR is approved or has the `ready` label, the PR author can also use the corresponding `/ci run`, `/ci retry`, and `/ci cancel` commands, or their `/amd-ci` variants. New commits do not start upstream CI automatically.

If you have any questions, please reach out to us on Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai.
